title: Dental PPO Plans Training Notes: Annual Maximum Limit on Reprocessed Initial-Wait Lines
content:
The annual-maximum limit on a Dental PPO Plans line reprocessed after a denial for the waiting period counted from the coverage effective date (a reprocessed initial-wait line) follows the person and the plan, and so decides the patient share on such a line.

**Rule.**
- For a person receiving the pediatric essential-health-benefit treatment (an individual exchange enrollment and a date of service before the person's 19th birthday, 19 being the pediatric age limit on every Dental PPO plan), no annual maximum applies.
- On a plan that banks rollover dollars (Premier 2000 and Elite 2500), the plan payment is never more than the remaining annual maximum plus the person's rollover balance (all rollover credits less all rollover draws); the part above the remaining annual maximum is paid from that balance.
- Otherwise the plan payment is never more than the remaining annual maximum.

The remaining annual maximum is the plan's annual maximum less the person's maximum postings net of maximum reversals for the line's benefit year.

**Questions and answers.**

*A 17-year-old on an individual exchange enrollment in Plus 1500 has used the whole annual maximum. Is the reprocessed line limited?* No. The person receives the pediatric treatment, so no annual maximum applies.

*The same person's line is dated on the 19th birthday.* The date of service is not before the 19th birthday, so the remaining annual maximum limits the payment.

*A Premier 2000 member has 46.10 of annual maximum remaining and a rollover balance of 300.00 (hypothetical); the payment before this limit is 128.40. What is paid?* The ceiling is 46.10 plus 300.00, which is 346.10, so 128.40 is paid: 46.10 within the annual maximum and 82.30 from the rollover balance.

*A Classic 1250 member in the same position, with no rollover?* The ceiling is the remaining annual maximum, 46.10.
